children: Indonesian stocks slipped 0.3% to 6,261 in early Wednesday trade, extending losses for a fourth straight session and notching their weakest level in six weeks.
Sentiment was weighed down by FTSE Russell’s move to upgrade Vietnam to emerging-market status from frontier, spurring a rebalancing of regional flows.
Caution also built ahead of Bank Indonesia’s policy decision later today, even as markets expect the benchmark rates to remain unchanged for a third month.
Still, a further drop in oil prices eased inflation worries, reflecting progress in U.S.–Iran diplomatic talks and capping the market downside.
President Prabowo, meanwhile,  hailed the government’s completion of IDR 218 trillion in bond repayments to the central bank, closing obligations dating back to the 1997–98 Asian financial crisis.
Losses were led by financials, tech, and property, with notable decliners Mitra Adiperkasa (-2.7%), Indosat (-2.1%), Alamtri Resources (-1.9%), and Indo Tambangraya Megah (-1.4%).

title: Indonesian Shares Extend Slide Before BI Rate Decision
